A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCLP-based role-play TTS research. All pages, equations, figures, tables, and appendices were readable and could be matched across versions, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original RP-TTS comparisons and reward ablations in Tables 2–3, subjective evaluations, and human–MCLP agreement analysis in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains and extends the original experiments, including additional baselines, human-rated ablations, cross-lingual metric validation, and stratified dataset analyses.

M1.justification: The MCLP formula and conditioning, SFT objective, GRPO procedure, and gated MCLP-plus-CER reward remain unchanged. However, v1 describes scorer-training loss on TA4 tokens, defined as interleaved text and audio, whereas v2 specifies audio-token-only loss. The unchanged Figure 1 and expanded Section 4.1 do not establish whether this reflects an actual loss-mask change or corrected documentation.

E1.justification: Appendix B extends metric evaluation beyond Mandarin RP-TTS to English and Mandarin Genshin-Voice speech, using self-prompted and preceding-utterance-prompted zero-shot synthesis. This adds language coverage and distinct prompting scenarios. The renamed WenetSpeech-RP-TTS corpus and Appendix C subdivisions retain the original main evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds four evaluated Instruct-TTS comparators: CosyVoice3, Higgs Audio V2, OV-InstructTTS, and Qwen3TTS, all without audio history. GPT-Audio, MiMo-Audio-7B-Instruct, and Step-Audio-2-mini remain, substantially broadening the comparison beyond general-purpose LALMs. Shortened MiMo labels do not identify a new baseline.

E3.justification: The evaluation drops Pinyin WER and adds CAM++ and Emo2Vec similarities. The MOS panel changes from 32 annotators with 30 valid responses to 50 with 48 valid responses, retaining 30 evaluation cases plus one quality-control case. SFT warmup is reported as 100 iterations instead of a 0.03 ratio, without establishing a rerun. Appendix B introduces a controlled self-versus-previous-prompt protocol using 1,000 samples per language from 20 speakers.

E4.justification: Table 3 extends the existing training-stage and reward ablations with human MOS and similarity metrics, directly testing perceptual benefits beyond MCLP. Appendix B adds cross-lingual prompting controls, while Appendix C analyzes dataset composition and performance by scene category, dialogue length, and speaker count. The original human–MCLP analysis and Figure 5 are retained and relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for MOS and the binned human–MCLP win rates. The correlation analysis retains 32 listeners and ten bins. New MOS rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; changed interval values and the larger subjective panel do not establish a new statistical estimation procedure. No seed or repeated-training-run reporting is added.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 add baseline, similarity, and ablation MOS results; Tables 4–9 add cross-lingual outcomes and dataset/performance breakdowns. The proposed system's MOS changes from 3.646 ± 0.060 to 3.576 ± 0.045 under the revised listener panel, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Shared CER and MCLP values remain unchanged, while Pinyin WER entries disappear. The retrieved-video count is corrected from 13,510 to 8,556, matching Table 1 in both versions.

T1.justification: v2 removes the entire information-theoretic justification in Section 4.1, including v1 Equations 2–3 linking MCLP, conditional entropy, and mutual information under a small-KL assumption. Operational explanations replace this formal argument without a replacement derivation. The metric and optimization equations otherwise remain, with renumbering.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain MCLP, its use in hybrid-reward RL, and the RP-TTS dataset. The conclusion broadens the claimed superiority from strong LALM baselines to both LALM and Instruct-TTS baselines. Human alignment receives greater prominence, but it was already claimed and investigated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of semantic tokenization, fixed-transcript conditioning, and the ground-truth prediction direction. It replaces v1's interpretation of MOS as approaching ground-truth naturalness with an explicit stylistic-consistency interpretation, and explains the limitations of similarity proxies and single-turn comparisons. New limitations identify Mandarin-focused evaluation, restricted domains, and possible noise or bias from automatic annotations.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future dataset release; v2 reports public code and supplies a dataset access link. It identifies the scorer's Step-Audio-2 initialization and substantially expands training documentation, including optimizer parameters, clipping, sequence length, minimum learning rate, and RL iteration, batch, warmup, and decoding settings. Most additions disclose previously unspecified details rather than demonstrate changed experiments. Appendix A's construction prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Higgs Audio V2, emotion2vec, CAM++, and 3D-Speaker. Its broader positioning relative to controllable TTS, speech role-playing agents, and RL remains substantially unchanged. The PromptTTS 2 preprint-to-publication update identifies the same work and is not an added citation.

P1.justification: The metric explanation and experimental narrative undergo substantial rewriting. Human–metric validation moves from the ablations into a dedicated subsection before the main results, and the ablations are reorganized around SFT, RL, and rewards. v2 also introduces a dedicated limitations section, standardizes CER terminology, and corrects the running title and author information.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains baseline-family grouping, additional rows, and revised metric columns; Table 3 gains similarity and MOS columns. Six new appendix tables display cross-lingual validation, dataset distributions, and stratified performance. These substantially expand and restructure the evidence presentation. The original five figures and dataset-pipeline table are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important empirical weaknesses: Table 2 adds relevant Instruct-TTS comparisons, and Table 3 provides human evidence for the central RL benefit, with SFT MOS 3.178 versus 3.576 after RL, reducing reliance on the optimized MCLP metric. Expanded implementation/access information and explicit limitations also improve reproducibility and interpretation. The formal mutual-information argument is withdrawn, scorer-loss wording remains ambiguous, and Appendix C has unreconciled training totals of 304,489 and 308,023. These shortcomings temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial improvement in support for the central empirical claims.
